title: Policy & Procedure on safety and health problems of the staff, including occupational health hazards
html:
• PURPOSE:
    • To provide protocol on health needs of the employees.
  • SCOPE:
    • This policy is applicable to all employees (permanent, temporary, probationary, trainee, student or on contract) of the Hospital.
  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Top Management
    • Administrator
    • Human Resources Department
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
    • HRM: Human Resource Management
  • DEFINITION:
    • Occupational health hazard:

The hazards to which an individual is exposed during the course of performance of his job. These include physical, chemical, biological, mechanical and psychosocial hazards.

    • Staff:

All personnel working in the organization including employees, ‘fee for Service’ medical professionals, part-time workers, contractual personnel and volunteers

  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH: NABH Standards for Hospitals
  • POLICY:
    • Each new entrant shall undergo pre-employment medical examination to make certain that she/he is fit to perform the duties to be assigned.
    • All hospital personnel injured by an occupational Percutaneous or mucous membrane exposure from a known or potentially infected source of HIV, HCV and HBsAg shall report to Casualty for evaluation and further action.
    • If the employee is not vaccinated or has failed to complete vaccination he shall be vaccinated for hepatitis B immunoglobulin vaccination and the amount shall be charged as per the Management policy prevailing.
    • Infection control nurse shall verify status in the Medical Report of the new entrant and shall coordinate for completion of immunization.
    • Periodic regular health checks shall be carried out minimum once a year for the staffs involved in the direct patient care.
    • Food and Beverage staff shall be subjected to periodic medical checkup for communicable diseases like TB, typhoid, cholera, hepatitis A etc.
    • Master list of staffs under them shall be prepared by following HOD’s for annual medical check-ups as per the scope of this process.
      • Personal Management as per the list of Medical Practitioners in the record
      • Kitchen manager
      • Housekeeping Supervisor
      • Nursing superintendents
    • Schedule:
      • Every year this medical check-up shall be organised in the month of January. Personal Management shall follow for the list to be obtained in the month of December and shall coordinate with Casualty to complete the task. All medical check-up records and actions shall be recorded in the personal file of the staff.
    • Control:
      • Infection control nurse shall audit 100% for compliance and shall resolve issue if any.
      • Clinical Audit shall monitor effective implementation.
  • PROCEDURE:
    • Pre-employment health Checkup:
      • Each new entrant shall undergo pre-employment medical examination to make certain that she / he is fit to perform the duties to be assigned.
      • Per-employment health checkup is the responsibility of employee; discounted health checkup package is offered by hospital.
      • Following tests are performed:
        • Complete blood count
        • HIV & HBS-Ag test
        • Blood group
        • ECG
        • Chest X-ray
        • Vision test
      • HIV test is done only after consent.
      • Reports are reviewed by Physician (Minimum MBBS qualification) & fitness certificate is issued.
    • Vaccinations:
      • All staffs in direct patient care are immunized for Hepatitis B.
      • Vaccines are provided after getting signed on consents only.
      • If the employee is not vaccinated previously or has failed to complete vaccination he / she shall be vaccinated for hepatitis B immunoglobulin vaccination
      • If any employee claims that he / she has been vaccinated, he / she has to give it in written; this declaration will be attached in personal file. Also HBS-Ag titer is checked for checking of effectiveness of vaccination & need to repeat.
      • Vaccinations for outbreaks like Swine flu (H1N1) will be provided by management time to time.
      • A record of vaccination is maintained by Infection Control Nurse.
      • Staff working in kitchen / dealing with food & beverages must be vaccinated for Hepatitis A & Typhoid.
      • Charges for vaccination:
        • For Hospital Employees: Charges will be borne by HOSPITAL management
        • For outsourced / contract staff: Charges will be borne by contractor.
    • Annual Health Checkup:
      • All staff working in hospital are screened in annual health checkup
      • Annual health checkup is the responsibility of management
      • Tests for staff in clinical area: Same as in pre-employment health checkup
      • Test for food handlers:
        • Complete Blood count
        • Urine routine
        • Stool examination
        • Eye checkup
        • Nasal & skin swabs (if advised by physician)
      • All medical check-up records and actions shall be recorded in the personal file of the staff.
    • Health benefits:
      • Employees are eligible to avail following discount policy in medical bill after providing one year of continuous service.
      • Employee includes person himself / herself
      • Dependent includes:
        • For male employees:

Wife, Parents & children not more than two (under 18 years of age)

        • For unmarried female candidates:

Parents

        • For married female candidates:

Husband & children not more than two (under 18 years of age)

      • Note:
        • Management reserves the rights of modifying & denying the services
        • No discount on affiliated services & tie up arrangements.
        • Health benefits for dependents will be as per discretion of management.
      • Health benefits includes:
ServiceEmployee
Admission in General Ward (Stay & Nursing Charges)Free
Pathology Charges15 % Discount
Radiology (X-ray / USG)50 % Discount
Radiology (CT / MRI scan)15 % Discount
Pharmacy & ConsumablesAt actual cost
    • Occupational Hazards:
      • Staffs are trained about prevention & management of occupational hazards.
      • Appropriate Personal Protective Equipments are provided.
      • All hospital personnel injured by an occupational percutaneous or mucous membrane exposure from a known or potentially infected source of HIV, HCV and HBs-Ag shall report to Casualty & infection control nurse for evaluation and further action.
      • Such staffs are screened for HIV, HCV and HBs-Ag periodically & treatment is given according to physician’s opinion.
